crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Invoice Capture and Coding
children.blurb: Invoice capture and coding covers the intake of supplier invoices from email, scan, or electronic feed and the conversion of those documents into structured records.

children.name: Customer Credit Risk
children.blurb: Customer credit risk is the chance that a business customer will not pay what it owes under agreed terms, and it sits on the receivables side of payables and receivables.

children.name: Programmable Settlement and Escrow
children.blurb: Programmable settlement and escrow covers the use of software rules to hold, release, and reconcile funds between parties in payables and receivables.

children.name: Collections and Payment Plans
children.blurb: Collections and payment plans cover the work of recovering overdue receivables and structuring scheduled payments, whether a customer needs an installment plan or a vendor needs a revised payables schedule.

children.name: Working Capital Timing
children.blurb: Working capital timing covers when cash actually moves in and out of a business, not just when an invoice is dated.

sections.body: This section of The AI Accountant covers money moving between companies: invoices, credit, settlement, collections, and working capital. AI is doing practical work here: reading invoices, extracting line items, matching purchase orders, coding to ledgers, predicting late payment, scoring customer credit, routing collections, and timing payments. It is not just chat but document understanding, anomaly detection, forecasting, and workflow automation. In payables, systems compare invoice text to contracts and receipts, flag duplicates, and suggest approval routes. In receivables, models rank accounts by risk, draft reminders, and propose payment plans. The site tracks 732 AI tools across its atlas, and this section sits within that wider catalogue.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Where work stands: invoice capture is largely solved for clean digital documents, with high accuracy on common fields. Matching and coding work well when purchase orders, receipts, and vendor masters are consistent. Credit risk remains harder, especially for small firms with little history and for sudden economic shifts. Collections automation can rank accounts and send reminders, but it cannot reliably resolve disputes or assess hardship. Settlement and escrow automation is limited by bank rails, legal finality, and cross border variation. The site's 222 compliance and regulation pages show how much of this work depends on local tax, privacy, and payment rules.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: Start with Invoice Capture and Coding, which is the entry point for payables data. Customer Credit Risk comes next, deciding whether to sell on terms and how much exposure to take. Programmable Settlement and Escrow covers the movement and conditional release of funds. The Collections and Payment Plans page deals with what happens after due date, including outreach and restructuring. Working Capital Timing ties these together by showing how payment terms, discounts, and cash conversion cycles affect liquidity. A reader would go to Invoice Capture and Coding for document processing, to Customer Credit Risk for underwriting, to Programmable Settlement and Escrow for payment mechanics, to Collections and Payment Plans for recovery, and to Working Capital Timing for the cash flow view.
